reading_scope: 16 sources have inspected method/theorem passages; R15 uses the original abstract and accessible original section-7 cache, with the population inequality independently rederived. No blanket full-paper-reading claim.

sources.title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations
sources.read: Section 3, Theorem 1 and scope of factorized-prior non-identifiability
sources.supports: Semantic factor identification requires explicit model/data assumptions.
sources.limit: Not an impossibility theorem for our supervised, typed memory; no segmentation gain guarantee.

sources.title: Weakly-Supervised Disentanglement Without Compromises
sources.read: Theorem 1 assumptions and section 4.1 pairwise constraints
sources.supports: Controlled pairs can constrain which factors should remain shared.
sources.limit: The theorem assumes a smooth invertible generator and population matching; occlusion is not invertible, so our pairs do not inherit identifiability.

sources.title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
sources.read: Sections 3.1-3.2, quantized lookup and gradient destinations around equation 3
sources.supports: Input-dependent lookup, reconstruction, dictionary and encoder objectives have distinct gradient paths.
sources.limit: Quantization alone does not ground a code as a pig part; its reported collapse claim is not universal for all codebooks.

sources.title: Task-Driven Dictionary Learning
sources.read: Sections III-A and IV-A, task-dependent sparse representation and Proposition 1 gradients
sources.supports: Dictionary reconstruction and downstream task learning are distinct objectives; task gradients must reach the representation.
sources.limit: Elastic-net differentiability assumptions do not establish global convergence for our nonlinear decoder and truncated retrieval.

sources.title: ProtoSeg: Interpretable Semantic Segmentation with Prototypical Parts
sources.read: Sections 3.1-3.3, similarity-based output, projection and same-class activation diversity
sources.supports: Prototype evidence can participate directly in dense prediction and retain training-patch references.
sources.limit: Semantic categories and activation diversity do not prove anatomical identity or distinguish adjacent pigs.

sources.title: Multi-Scale Grouped Prototypes for Interpretable Semantic Segmentation
sources.publication: arXiv 2409.09497, inspected v2 dated 2025-04-28; venue not asserted
sources.read: Sections 3.1-3.3 and appendix sections 16-17; simplex weights and weighted geometric grouping
sources.supports: Multi-scale evidence grouping and interpretable composition; also documents texture-driven failure.
sources.limit: A visible-part conjunction needs an occlusion treatment in our task; its groups are not guaranteed anatomical or instance-specific.

sources.title: Matrix Capsules with EM Routing
sources.read: Sections 2-3, part-whole pose votes and EM routing procedures
sources.supports: Explicit attachment transforms and agreement between part votes offer a mathematical composition mechanism.
sources.limit: Not evidence for transplanting a full capsule network into dense pig segmentation; articulation and occlusion remain additional conditions.

sources.title: Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention
sources.supports: Competition over entities and permutation-consistent assignments are useful distinct objects of computation.
sources.limit: Our normal instances remain fixed detector rows; no learned-slot detector or global pixel exclusivity is automatically introduced.

sources.title: Compositional Convolutional Neural Networks: A Deep Architecture With Innate Robustness to Partial Occlusion
sources.read: Primary PDF cached method sections 3.1-3.2, equations 1-13; direct PDF fetch timed out
sources.supports: Separate object and occluder likelihoods and viewpoint mixtures explain visible evidence without forcing absent parts negative.
sources.limit: Classification evidence is not visible-instance Mask AP evidence; our responsibility equations use explicit stated mixture assumptions.

sources.title: MagicPony: Learning Articulated 3D Animals in the Wild
sources.read: Sections 3.1-3.2 and multi-viewpoint discussion; template, deformation, articulation and image feature roles
sources.supports: Canonical content, instance deformation and viewpoint are distinct functional variables.
sources.limit: No extra frozen encoder or full 3D reconstruction task is automatically adopted; single-image hidden anatomy is not uniquely determined.

sources.title: Supervised Contrastive Learning
sources.supports: Positive and negative sets must reflect the intended semantic equivalence.
sources.limit: Different pigs can be positives for anatomy but competitors for ownership; no general contrastive loss is activated solely from this citation.

sources.title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
sources.read: Sections 2 and 4.2, selective risk/coverage and ungated auxiliary objective
sources.supports: A selector needs training evidence outside the currently selected subset.
sources.limit: We return the native prediction instead of abstaining; forced memory coverage is not an objective or guarantee.

sources.title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
sources.read: Sections 3-4, Propositions 1-2 and section 5.2 mixture-surrogate inconsistency
sources.supports: Cost-sensitive action selection compares conditional expected costs rather than confidence or majority wins.
sources.limit: Population consistency for specified costs does not prove finite-neural optimization, AP consistency or out-of-domain safety.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
sources.read: Section 4.2, temperature scaling equation 9 and calibration discussion
sources.supports: Confidence and correctness differ; temperature scaling preserves class ranking.
sources.limit: A low-entropy lookup is not a calibrated pig-part match; native detector scores remain frozen.

sources.title: A theory of learning from different domains
sources.read: Primary abstract and accessible original section-7 cache on ideal joint error and weighting; full theorem passage unavailable in this review
sources.supports: Target labels and shared attainable rules matter in addition to input-domain resemblance.
sources.limit: The population binary inequality is independently rederived in our note; no numerical domain bound or AP theorem claimed.

sources.title: Implicit Geometric Regularization for Learning Shapes
sources.read: Section 3, Eikonal equations 2-3 and finite-penalty/solution-uniqueness caveats
sources.supports: Signed-distance behavior depends on geometric conditions rather than naming a field SDF.
sources.limit: Adding a finite Eikonal penalty does not certify our raster field or geometric displacement; no automatic new loss.

sources.title: The Lovasz-Softmax loss: A tractable surrogate for the optimization of the intersection-over-union measure in neural networks
sources.read: Sections 1-2 and 3.1, Jaccard set loss and surrogate construction
sources.supports: Pixel log loss, per-mask IoU and aggregate evaluation objectives are distinct.
sources.limit: Its semantic IoU surrogate is not a COCO instance-AP guarantee or authorization to change loss after results.
